description: Whether two topic labels name the same subject. Merging is the decision that cannot be reviewed by reading the prompt: too strict and one subject spreads across rows that never reach the promotion threshold, too loose and every specific question in a domain collapses into one useless bucket. These are the pairs that mark the boundary. Every example here is invented — none of it comes from a real workspace, and none of it should.

cases.name: rephrasing
cases.why: Two wordings for one thing. They share almost no characters, so only the model tier can settle it.

cases.name: elaboration
cases.why: One side carries a qualifier the other drops; it is still the same subject.

cases.name: harmless qualifier
cases.why: "issue" does not change the subject itself.

cases.name: abbreviation
cases.why: An abbreviation and its expansion are one thing, with barely any character overlap.

cases.name: specific lookup inside a broad subject
cases.incoming: last month GRN numbers for warehouse 3
cases.why: It does sit in the same area, but it is one lookup rather than a standing interest. Folding it in turns the interest list into a bucket that holds everything.

cases.name: different question in the same domain
cases.why: Two different concerns about the same endpoint.

cases.name: hyponym
cases.why: A narrower concept is not the same thing, or one broad subject would swallow a whole domain.

cases.name: two aspects of one thing
cases.why: Two stages of the same exercise, and they are about different things. Pairs like this really were merged in production.

cases.name: broad subject versus a lookup in it
cases.why: Running an event and checking who signed up are two different things. Pairs like this really were merged in production.

cases.name: unrelated
cases.why: Nothing in common; no tier should merge these.

cases.name: same word different field
cases.why: Sharing the word "partition" is not a relationship.

granularity.note: A subject has to be a recurring AREA, not one question. Put a name, a number, a date, a version or a quantity in the label and it can only ever match itself: counted once, stuck at one hit forever, and the threshold means nothing.

cases.question: Which GRN numbers did warehouse 3 log last month?
cases.bad: warehouse 3 March 2026 GRN number lookup log

cases.question: What is the default page size on the v2.3 orders API?
cases.bad: v2.3 orders API default page size lookup

cases.question: Who is the business contact for the settlement platform?
cases.bad: settlement platform business contact lookup log
